status_summary: The Fed's main operative decisions in the period ran opposite to a wind-down. On 2025-10-29 the FOMC announced it would stop reducing its securities holdings on 2025-12-01, and on 2025-12-10 it began reserve management purchases of Treasury bills (from 2025-12-11) to keep reserves ample. Two elements match the chapter: paydowns of agency mortgage-backed securities are reinvested into Treasury bills, so those holdings run off without replacement, and reserve management purchases are limited to Treasury securities. Total assets were about $6.74 trillion on 2026-09-30 (Treasuries $4.56 trillion, mortgage-backed securities $1.90 trillion), compared with the chapter's figure of nearly $9 trillion, and the Fed still pays interest on reserve balances (3.90 percent from 2026-09-17). On 2026-07-09 the Fed announced a balance sheet policy task force to assess the approach, but the September 2026 directive did not change course.

timeline.event: FOMC announced it would stop reducing its securities holdings on 2025-12-01, ending the runoff program.

FOMC directed reserve management purchases of Treasury bills (and other Treasuries of three years or less if needed) starting 2025-12-11 to keep reserves ample, and reinvestment of agency securities paydowns into Treasury bills.

Fed announced a Balance Sheet Policy task force (co-led by Karen Dynan, Raghuram Rajan and Jeremy Stein) to assess the costs, benefits and institutional effects of the current approach and report to the FOMC.
Implementation note set interest on reserve balances at 3.90 percent effective 2026-09-17, continued rollover of Treasury principal and reserve management purchases as appropriate.
H.4.1 release of 2026-10-01 shows total assets of about $6.74 trillion, Treasury securities $4.56 trillion, mortgage-backed securities $1.90 trillion and reserve balances $2.95 trillion.

title: Shrink the Fed balance sheet, hold only Treasuries, and end interest on reserves
uncertainties: I did not verify the balance sheet size at the start of the period (January 2025), so I cannot state how much of the decline from the chapter's roughly $9 trillion occurred before 2025; the H.4.1 link is the rolling current release and will change. The stage reflects the October 2025 end of runoff and December 2025 purchases being opposite to the chapter's wind-down, while the shift of mortgage paydowns into Treasury bills and the July 2026 task force point partly the other way. The pace of runoff in 2025 before December was not read.
